beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Compare money by finding which group is worth more or less.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A group is a set. Its value is how much money it is worth.

do.text: Value: how much it is worth

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: *B* has more coins, so *B* has more money.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Two dimes are in set *A*. Each dime is worth ten cents. This sign means cents.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Ten plus ten makes twenty cents.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: *B* has three nickels. Each nickel is worth five cents.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Five, ten, fifteen cents: the whole set’s value.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One dime trades for two nickels. Both are worth ten cents.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Trade the other dime. Four nickels keep the total at twenty cents.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Match equal values.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three pairs match, with one extra nickel in *A*.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Two dimes are worth more than three nickels here.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Try one quarter against two dimes and four pennies. Each penny is worth one cent.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Six coins must be more than one coin.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Count the dimes in *B*: ten, twenty cents.

do.text: Count the value of Set B.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Add each penny: twenty-one, twenty-two, twenty-three, twenty-four cents.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The quarter is worth twenty-five cents, one cent more.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Back to our first sets: add a one-dollar bill to *A*, making one dollar and twenty cents.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A five-dollar bill gives *B* five dollars and fifteen cents.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Bills count by value. Compare whole dollars first, then cents if dollars match.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Most means greatest, least means smallest, and exactly means the same amount.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Two dimes beat three nickels: twenty cents is more than fifteen.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One quarter beats six coins: twenty-five cents is more than twenty-four.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: With bills, five dollars and fifteen cents is more than one dollar and twenty cents.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: More coins does not always mean more money. Count the value, then compare.
